newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees record 20 mln hectares hit by drought.
newsitem.headline: China sees record 20 mln hectares hit by drought.

text.p: A record 20 million hectares of arable land have been hit by drought in China's north while floods have damaged 4.4 million hectares in the south, the China Daily said on Thursday.
"China may experience a year of disasters which are likely to occur simultaneously," the newspaper quoted Vice Premier Jiang Chunyun as saying.

Persistent sweltering heat in the north and floods in the south are threatening the main autumn grain crop with just 80 to 100 days before the harvest, Jiang said. More than 70 percent of China's grain is gathered in the autumn.
Since June, areas north of the Yangtze river have been hurt by unusually high temperatures and a 40 to 60 percent drop in rainfall.
Floods in the south have hit unseasonally early.
The drought would affect this year's corn crop but would not cut the overall grain harvest below forecast levels, an agricultural official said on Wednesday.
Officials have forecast grain output for this year at more than 484 million tonnes, compared with a record 490 million tonnes last year.
Officials say they are still hoping for a third successive bumper harvest.
Local governments have so far invested 2.2 billion yuan ($265 million) and mobilised 38 million people daily to fight the drought and to carry out measures to prevent flooding, the China Daily said.
